title: DOE ARPA-E Launches $37 Million QC3 Program Across Ten Quantum Chemistry Performers
key_facts: $37 million across ten selected teams over three years
Program directed by Dr. Jyotsna Sharma
Goal: 100-fold speedup over classical, validated at about 100 logical qubits
Applicants had to partner with quantum hardware providers
QuEra is exclusive hardware partner for LBNL, LLNL and Phasecraft
Builds on LLNL's $4.1 million MAGNETIQC award; QuEra targets 1,000 logical qubits by 2029
quote_evidence: The U.S. Department of Energy's Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy (ARPA-E) has officially launched its Quantum Computing for Computational Chemistry (QC3) program, directing $37 million across ten selected research teams over three years.

Neutral-atom quantum developer QuEra Computing was selected as the exclusive external QPU hardware and algorithm co-design partner for three of the non-hardware prime performers (LBNL, LLNL, and Phasecraft).
why_it_matters_hint: US government is funding a test of quantum computing on energy chemistry.
